title: Bean foliage beetle in common beans

Header: Bean foliage beetle in common beans
Ootheca spp. ; Monolepta spp. Kirombosho in Swahili, Kirombosho in Kichaga, Kiindi in Kisambaa, Nasheve in Kipare, Lwenya in Kinyakyusa, Nadolukunya in Kimaasai

Prevention: Rotate with non-legumes, e.g. with maize, sunflower, sorghum, etc.
Or intercrop with these non- host crops.
Post-harvest tillage to destroy larvae and adults that are dormant in the soil.
Delay sowing for 1 - 2 weeks during cropping season (e.g. mid-March instead of early
Note that in case of bean fly infestation, a contrary 1-2 week earlier planting is advised.
Improve soil fertility to encourage foliage growth, and to improve ability of plants to recover from damage.
Monitoring: Scout once per week at early stages of bean growth.
At 1 – 4 adult beetles per square meter consider direct control measure.
Foliage beetles chew small round holes in the leaves.

When already few feeding holes are observed on half of the leaves per plant, consider green direct control action is considered (this equals score 3-4 of severity on the common 1-10 leaf damage scale).
Chemical control may be considered if many holes are seen on many plants.
Search for bean yellowing and shrivelling that might be a result of larval root damage.
To be sure it is larval damage and not another pest or disease, sample soil around several of these bean plants.
Search at a depth of 5 – 15 cm for small whitish larvae. 3 -8 larvae per square meter justify post-harvest ploughing to reduce pest populations prior next cropping season.
Direct Control: Neem seed cake powders at a rate of 25g/ litre of water.
This repels adult beetles from feeding on bean leaves.
Apply a maximum of two times at 7 to 10 day intervals.
Post-harvest tillage to expose larvae to the sun and kill them, reducing the pest populations’ carryover to the next cropping season.
Azadirachtin products (Nimbecidine, Neem oils, and others)
Restrictions: There are no feasible chemical sprays against the
Ootheca larvae onto or into the soil.; Against the adult beetles foliar sprays are possible if threshold is reached.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.; Farmers are not allowed to buy and use
Ia, Ib, II products without special permits (Plant
Tanzania); Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (MAFC / TPRI).
WHO, but considered unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use; moulting disruptor pesticide group which also inhibits egg laying, and has antifeedant effects; p.h.i. 3 d; r.e.i. 1 d.
